For a pure component or other congruently melting compound, this is observed in thermal analysis as a temperature arrest during the reaction. For non-congruent melting, the interfacial reaction temperature is not isothermal, thus the appearance of the reaction in thermal analysis curves is commensurately altered. The reader is directed to W. Boettinger et al. (2006) for additional information regarding the appearance and underlying meaning of these curves. Since the assessment may be considered semi-quantitative for the enthalpy of fusion, the contribution here must be in terms of justification for a model of behavior rather than an accurate emperical description. Use of an admixture model between terminal species of the same crystal structure is a common approach to estimating the enthalpy of fusion for different alloys (Mills 2005). The data obtained here would indicate that an axmixture model is a useful and justified assumption, though we are not currently able to comment deeply on the relative accuracy of said model. A more complete set of notes regarding the nature of the enthalpy measurements and corrections is given in the methods portion of this document. The change in primary phase (U-Mo to Mo) at Mo concentrations ⪆13.5 wt.% Mo would also alter the expression of the heat of fusion, making the measurements performed at higher Mo concentration less meaningful. Additionally, any microsegregation will result in melting or solidification of a range of alloy compositions. Since mass balance is a reasonable baseline, it is being assumed here that the instantaneous change in enthalpy per mole solidified or melted may appropriately be averaged over the entire reaction utilizing an assessment similar to that given in the model applications section. In short, the microsegregation effect on enthalpy presentation where initial freezing of higher Mo content dendrites (and lower Mo content interdendritic volume) is assumed to be equal in this analysis and is not further corrected. A more detailed coupling of the heat expression curves and microstructure characterization could lead to further shifts in the data.
